subject: AP routing: invoice vs card — clarification & next steps
messages:

Subject: AP routing: invoice vs card — clarification & next steps

Hi Jordan — great to meet you and the procurement team today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap:
- Demo: showed low-latency hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private deployment options.
- Estimated monthly run-rate you mentioned: $18k–$30k depending on pilot scale and burst capacity.
- Primary gating question: vendor onboarding / AP process — PO required vs. corporate card? Marketplace as an alternative was mentioned.

Questions for Procurement (to confirm):
1) Does GreenForge require a PO for all new vendors above $10k annual spend, or is the policy a higher threshold?
2) If PO required, what is the typical vendor setup timeline (W-9, insurance certs, banking details)?
3) Would you consider a short-term card payment (P-Card) while vendor onboarding runs in parallel? Any single-transaction or monthly limits?

Next steps I propose:
- If PO path: we provide vendor onboarding package (W-9, COI, bank info) + draft SOW for signature. Expect onboarding 3–5 business days once docs are complete; AP payment timing depends on your cycle.
- If card path: we can accommodate corporate card for pilot; need to confirm limits and invoicing cadence.
- Marketplace: if you purchase via a marketplace/reseller it often short-circuits vendor setup — do you have a preferred marketplace partner we should check with?

I attached a one-page SOW stub and a vendor checklist to speed review — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement to walk through. Are you available for a 30-minute procurement sync on Thursday (9/9) at 10am PT?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Parks <jordan.parks@greenforge.com>

Date: Tue, 07 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: AP routing: invoice vs card — clarification & next steps

Aditya — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from procurement: 

- PO policy: We require formal POs for new vendors when projected annual spend exceeds $25k. Below that, the procurement card (P-Card) is typically used.
- Onboarding timeline: vendor setup is usually 2–4 weeks after we receive a complete packet (W-9, signed SOW/contract, COI). The longest hold is usually procurement verification + vendor banking confirmation.
- P-Card limits: individual cardholders have $5k single-transaction limit, but we can route through finance for higher one-offs if needed.
- Marketplace: if Redwood is listed on one of our approved marketplaces (e.g., Azure Marketplace, AWS Marketplace), we can often pay via cloud procurement and avoid vendor onboarding — that would be ideal to speed the pilot.

I can join a call on Thursday 9/9 at 11am ET (8am PT). If you need 10am PT, I can try to shift. In the meantime, can you confirm whether Redwood is currently in any of the major cloud marketplaces, or if the reseller path is an option? Also please send the vendor packet to procurement@greenforge.com.

Best,
Jordan Parks
Head of Procurement, GreenForge Energy
procurement@greenforge.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Jordan — really helpful, thank you. Quick responses and an operational plan: 

Marketplace status:
- Redwood is currently listed on the Redwood-hosted partner marketplace and we have integrations with select cloud marketplaces, but we are not yet on GreenForge's approved vendor list. We can prioritize reseller marketplace checks (Azure/AWS) this week — if GreenForge can accept marketplace procurement, that will be the fastest route.

If PO is required:
- We will send the completed vendor packet (W-9, COI, bank info) to procurement@greenforge.com today.
- Draft SOW attached (GreenForge_SOW_v1.pdf) — terms are standard for a pilot: 3-month pilot, up to X tokens/month baseline, add-on billing for overage.
- Estimated vendor setup: 3–10 business days depending on your internal verification.

If card path (short-term pilot):
- We can accept a corporate card for initial invoices up to the P-Card limits. If you need higher single payments, we can invoice and you can route payment through AP (may take one billing cycle).
- Alternative: a short prepaid commitment (credit against usage) to start immediately while vendor setup completes. This reduces friction and preserves your P-Card limits.

Proposed immediate actions (please confirm):
1) I will send vendor packet + SOW to procurement@greenforge.com (today).
2) Procurement to confirm whether marketplace purchase is acceptable — Jordan, you to confirm vendor list check.
3) If marketplace not an option, we schedule a 30m procurement sync (Thu 9/9).

I attached the SOW and onboarding checklist again. If you prefer, Marissa (cc'd) is our enablement lead and can walk procurement through the vendor packet on the call.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai

Hi Jordan — thanks for the quick responses. Two quick clarifications from our ops team and the attachments I promised: 

1) Vendor packet contents (attached): W-9 (completed), COI template, vendor banking form.
2) Typical commercial timeline for pilot:
   - Day 0: Vendor packet submitted + SOW signed (electronic signature).
   - Day 1–3: Internal validation and insurance cert verification.
   - Day 4–10: Banking verification and AP setup; invoice payable on next cycle depending on your payment terms.

Temporary options while onboarding is in-progress:
- Prepaid credit (we invoice and apply as credit to start the pilot immediately).
- Use of P-Card for monthly invoices if under your card limits.
- Reseller/marketplace purchase (faster if acceptable).

Please see attached: Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.xlsx and GreenForge_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW has placeholders for trial limits and billing cadence). If GreenForge confirms marketplace purchase is okay, we'll prioritize that path. Otherwise, once we get the signed SOW and W-9 back, we'll kick off onboarding and share an internal onboarding tracker.

Action items: 
- Jordan/procurement: confirm marketplace OK or confirm PO path and preferred SOW signature method (DocuSign vs emailed PDF).
- Aditya/Marissa: follow up with any missing vendor details and schedule Thu 9/9 8am PT procurement sync if requested.
